working_title: Scotland's Golf Coast: A Practical Guide to Playing East Lothian
angle: East Lothian is often treated as a side-trip from St Andrews, but it packs more world-class links per square mile than anywhere else in Scotland — all within an hour of Edinburgh. This post cuts through the bucket-list noise and gives a regular club golfer a realistic picture of what to play, what to skip if time is tight, and what to expect on the ground.
research_notes:
- East Lothian is officially known as Scotland's 'Golf Coast' and has more championship links per square mile than anywhere else in the country (VisitScotland / multiple sources)
- Over 21 courses in the region, including Muirfield, North Berwick West Links, Gullane (three courses), The Renaissance Club, Dunbar, Archerfield, Craigielaw, Kilspindie, and The Glen (Gilmerton House / top100golfcourses.com)
- Muirfield: ranked 6th in Golf Digest's World's 100 Greatest in 2025; unique concentric-loop layout means wind hits from all angles; visitor access strictly limited to two days a week — tee times extremely competitive (GolfBreaks / Birdie Brae / golf.com)
- North Berwick West Links: ranked 9th in Golf Digest's World's 100 Greatest in 2025; historic, quirky design with stone walls, blind shots, and the famous 'Redan' par-3 (4th hole) that has been copied worldwide (GolfBreaks / marineandlawn.com)
- Gullane No.1: former host of the Scottish Open; three Gullane courses available to visitors; iconic 7th hole offers panoramic views of the Firth of Forth; 'very underrated and often overshadowed by nearby Muirfield and North Berwick' (todays-golfer.com)
- Kilspindie: described as 'an East Lothian sleeper, a quirky charmer set hard beside the sea' (golf.com) — good lower-cost option
- Craigielaw: newer course, often overlooked, with good practice facilities (marineandlawn.com)
- Dunbar: accessible, good-value championship-standard course at east end of the region (top100golfcourses.com)
- Common visitor mistake: booking only the famous names and missing value venues like The Glen or Luffness New (top100golfcourses.com)
- Coastal microclimate: reportedly drier than surrounding areas — worth noting for trip planning (top100golfcourses.com — treat this as a general claim, don't cite a specific rainfall figure unless verified)
- Edinburgh Airport is roughly one hour's drive from the region (top100golfcourses.com)
- Transport: car hire or minibus strongly recommended; courses spread along the coastline (Gilmerton House / GolfBreaks)
- Booking: championship courses like Muirfield and North Berwick fill up fast, especially in peak season — early booking essential (GolfBreaks / Gilmerton House)
- Green fees (from Birdie Brae — include in post with caveat that fees change seasonally and should be confirmed before booking): Kilspindie from ~£55; Dunbar ~£140; Gullane No.1 ~£225; North Berwick West ~£255; Renaissance Club ~£350 peak; Muirfield ~£395 visitor rate. Do NOT present these as definitive — flag to human editor to verify current rates before publish.
- The Open Championship returns to St Andrews in July 2027, which may spike interest in Scottish golf trips from 2026 onwards — a useful hook for timeliness
must_avoid:
- Do not fabricate or present green fees as confirmed current prices — the Birdie Brae figures are a useful steer for the brief but must be flagged as approximate and verified by a human before the post is published; present them in the draft as 'broadly in the range of' or similar, not as exact current rates
- No affiliate links to golf tour operators or booking platforms unless they appear in approved-partners.md — flag any operator mentions (e.g. Golfbreaks, 8AM Travel) in draft notes for human review

- No medical/injury advice beyond standard warm-up guidance
- No gambling, betting, or financial-advice framing around trip budgeting — describe costs factually only
- Avoid the phrase 'hidden gem' (clichéd and inaccurate for a region this well-known); same for 'bucket list' as a crutch
- Do not imply East Lothian is unknown or undiscovered — it is well-regarded; the angle is practical planning, not discovery
